paper.title_en: Investigation of antimagnetic rotation in the <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>46</mn></mrow></math> odd-<math><mi>A</mi></math> isotones <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Rb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>83</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>85</mn></mmultiscripts></math>
paper.abstract_en: The possible antimagnetic rotation in the <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>46</mn></mrow></math> odd-<math><mi>A</mi></math> isotones <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Rb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>83</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>85</mn></mmultiscripts></math> is investigated using the cranked shell model combined with a particle-number-conserving method. For the positive-parity yrast bands in the two isotones, the angular-momentum alignments are reproduced well. The configurations of high-spin part in both bands are determined as <math><mrow><mi>π</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>⊗</mo><mi>ν</mi><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></math>, by analyzing the occupation probability of each cranked Nilsson orbital near the Fermi surface. The calculated <math><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>E</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> values are small and decrease with the increasing rotational frequency, in agreement with the experiments; meanwhile, the two-shears-like mechanism is exhibited clearly. Therefore, the high-spin parts of the two bands, built on <math><mrow><mi>π</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>⊗</mo><mi>ν</mi><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></math> configuration, match the criteria of antimagnetic rotation, which is the first time that the antimagnetic rotation is revealed for odd-<math><mi>A</mi></math> nuclei in the <math><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>80</mn></mrow></math> mass region.
